source.data_role: retrospective replay of previously selected published effect summaries
limitations: Not raw single-cell training, new sequencing, or a prospective biological validation.
The distributed archive was target/gene-selected using original study results; this is a conditional archive-level benchmark.
Measurement SE does not measure extrapolation uncertainty or prove interval calibration.
Sparse fixed annotations are only a baseline; unannotated targets can have identical features.
Archive baseline is excluded: DE baseMean is not established pre-intervention expression.
No individual donor, dose, or biological time is invented from pooled summaries.

protocol.held_out_unit: perturbation target (all three condition summaries stay together)

feature_support.description: Fixed pathway/network priors only. No contrast-derived baseMean or response values used as inputs.

current_metrics.baseline: Training outcome means; no fitting on validation labels.
limitations: Group independence follows supplied group_id values; it is not proof of donor or study independence.
Retrospective prediction metrics do not establish prospective experiment value or causality.
Gaussian interval coverage is a diagnostic, not a claim of calibrated biological uncertainty.
Repeated reuse of one validation set can overfit the gate; reserve an untouched final test set.
A gate decision never promotes or overwrites the current model automatically.

Retrospective replay of a selected, processed public summary archive; not raw single-cell foundation-model training.
Targets are held out; donors and the original study are NOT independent across splits.
The parent archive already selected targets/genes using global data, so this is not an unbiased discovery benchmark.
Sparse prior annotations make most targets indistinguishable. A fitted surrogate is not evidence of general mechanism learning.
Blood CD4 T cell evidence does not establish liver or spleen response accuracy.
A rejection is retained as a real result; the held-out test does not change the gate or hyperparameters.
